title: What is a PLC?
summary: Meet the industrial computer that runs machines: what it does, what it is made of and why it is different from a PC.
objectives: Describe what a PLC does in one sentence
Name the parts of a PLC system

sections.heading: A computer for machines
sections.body: A **programmable logic controller (PLC)** reads signals from a machine, decides what to do with a program, and switches the machine's actuators. It does this over and over, many times per second, for years without rebooting. Buttons, switches and sensors are its **inputs**; motors, valves and lamps are driven by its **outputs**.

sections.heading: The control loop
sections.body: Every automated machine has the same shape: sensors tell the PLC what is happening, the program decides, actuators change the process, and the sensors see the result.
sections.diagram:
[ sensors ] --> [ INPUTS ]
                      |
                  [ PROGRAM ]   <- written by you
                      |
  [ actuators] <-- [ OUTPUTS ]
       |                      ^
       +----> [ MACHINE ] ----+

sections.heading: A real example
sections.body: A conveyor: a Start button and a Stop button are inputs, the motor contactor and a run lamp are outputs. The program decides that the motor runs after Start until Stop is pressed.

sections.heading: Common misconception
sections.body: A PLC does not 'listen' for button presses like a phone app. It **looks** at all inputs at the start of every cycle. If something happens between two looks, it only notices it at the next look.

sections.heading: Check yourself
sections.body: Which of these is an output?

question.question: Which device is driven by a PLC output?
question.explanation: Contactors, valves and lamps are actuators driven by outputs; sensors and buttons are inputs.

sections.heading: Look inside a simple panel
sections.body: Open the I/O training panel: two buttons, a selector, a sensor and three lamps wired to a compact PLC.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
A PLC is an industrial computer that cyclically reads inputs, runs a program and writes outputs.

**Troubleshooting note:** When a machine misbehaves, first ask: is the PLC seeing the right inputs, and is it deciding what you expect?

checkpoint.question: What does a PLC do repeatedly?
options: Read inputs, run the program, write outputs
checkpoint.explanation: This read-execute-write cycle is the scan cycle.

checkpoint.question: Why are PLCs used instead of office PCs?
options: They are built for harsh environments and continuous operation
checkpoint.explanation: Robustness and deterministic cyclic operation matter in industry.
